decisions.statement: A change is judged before the change reaches disk.
A refused change leaves nothing behind.
A change may land with no check run.
The checks judging a change are the checks the change leaves rather than every check filed.
Audit judges every page.
The other phases judge only the changed pages.
A check's answer is undone by a change to the input the check runs on.
A check's answer is undone by a change to the input the check runs with.
A change runs a check for a change to the input the check runs on.
A change to the input a check runs with leaves the pages already landed unjudged.
Such a page is judged when that page is next changed.
Such a page is judged where the check is asked for by name.
Every check names its input.
Every check is cheap enough to run at change.
A check's ceiling is stated in time rather than in processes alive.
Every check runs at change unless Alan has that check off.
Every check that runs at change runs at deploy.
An input wider than the answer rests on costs a run that finds nothing.
An input narrower than the answer rests on loses a refusal for good.
A check reads the index together with the change rather than the index alone.
A check no change ran is unmeasured rather than sound.
A check a process could not finish is unmeasured rather than refusing.
An unmeasured check is counted and told apart from a check that refused.
An unmeasured answer is not carried to a later commit.
What leaves a check unmeasured is a condition of the machine rather than of the input.
No check judges the imports a repository outside akasha takes from inside akasha.
No check judges whether a change made a decision on another page false.
No check but the compiler check exists only to test the claims the compiler tests.
A check that only repeats the compiler does not land.
A run is held to the ceiling stated for the code that ran, and a run at deploy to the audit group's.

definition: how a change is judged against what must be true of it

directives.name: Do The Work
directives.act: Never add a check for a set of work to be completed; complete the work instead.
directives.warrant: A check with nothing left to catch reads like one still working, and every author pays for it.
aids: Ask whether a new violation can arrive tomorrow.
Never refuse a check for arriving in a migration.

directives.name: Removal First
directives.act: Establish that a check still earns its place before making it faster or more correct.
directives.warrant: No check is faster or more correct than one that is not there, and a repair is always available.
aids: Even a small speedup asks the question first.
Never take a check's age for its worth.

directives.name: Superseded Reach
directives.act: Weigh a check that duplicates a gate by what that gate does not reach, never by what it repeats.
directives.warrant: The repetition is what a reader sees, so removal reads as obvious while the gap goes unnamed.
aids: Write down what the gate misses before deciding.
Cut the part of the check the gate reaches.

directives.name: Header By Hand
directives.act: Repair a header that has gone false by hand, never by gating prose against the code beneath it.
directives.warrant: A header is false only against code the reader has in mind and the text never names.
aids: Never delete the header instead of fixing it.
Never repair it by copying the code beneath.
